s1.syndrome_frame: A toddler with a chronic skin eruption characterized by multiple annular, indurated, dusky red plaques with central clearing and trailing scale, accompanied by fever and otitis media
salient_findings: Multiple annular, indurated, dusky red plaques with central clearing and trailing scale
Perivascular and periadnexal infiltrate of cells with homogeneous chromatin and abundant cytoplasm on histopathology
Elevated white blood cell count of 76,400/µL
key_facts: The eruption began 2 months previously
The patient has a history of neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) and juvenile xanthogranulomas
The patient was treated with griseofulvin and clotrimazole without improvement
The patient developed fever and was diagnosed with otitis media one day prior to presentation
The patient is currently taking acetaminophen, ibuprofen, and amoxicillin
There is no family history of NF1
Scattered café au lait macules are present on the back
Histopathology showed positive staining for CD33, CD123, CD4, and CD163
Laboratory tests revealed an elevated white blood cell count

differentials: Plasma Cell Myeloma with Cutaneous Involvement
per_call: Plasma Cell Myeloma with Cutaneous Involvement

shortlist.label: Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Positive staining for CD4 and CD163, and presence of café au lait macules

shortlist.label: Juvenile Xanthogranuloma
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's history of juvenile xanthogranulomas and presence of skin lesions with central clearing

shortlist.label: Lymphomatoid Papulosis
shortlist.why_kept: Skin lesions with central clearing and presence of atypical lymphocytes

shortlist.label: Myeloproliferative Neoplasm
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated white blood cell count and presence of systemic symptoms such as fever

shortlist.label: Chronic Myelomonocytic Leukemia
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated white blood cell count and presence of monocytic proliferation in histopathology

raw.rationale: The patient's histopathology results showing positive staining for CD33, CD123, CD4, and CD163, along with the presence of perivascular and periadnexal infiltrate, are consistent with Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis. Additionally, the patient's history of neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) and the presence of café au lait macules are also associated with this condition.

rejected.label: Juvenile Xanthogranuloma
rejected.why: The patient already has a history of juvenile xanthogranuloma, but the current presentation and histopathology results do not support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Lymphomatoid Papulosis
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and histopathology results do not match the typical features of lymphomatoid papulosis, which usually presents with papular lesions and atypical lymphocytes on histology.

rejected.label: Myeloproliferative Neoplasm
rejected.why: While the patient has an elevated white blood cell count, the histopathology results and clinical presentation do not support a diagnosis of myeloproliferative neoplasm.

rejected.label: Chronic Myelomonocytic Leukemia
rejected.why: The patient's age and clinical presentation are not consistent with chronic myelomonocytic leukemia, which is a rare condition typically seen in older adults.
